newsitem.title: USA: Johnson & Johnson withdraws CONFIDE service.
newsitem.headline: Johnson & Johnson withdraws CONFIDE service.

text.p: Johnson & Johnson said on Thursday that its CONFIDE HIV Testing and Counseling Service is being withdrawn from the market, effective immediately, due to lack of consumer demand.
"After a year on the market, the usage level of CONFIDE is quite low," said Robert B. Miller, president of Johnson & Johnson's Direct Access Diagnostics unit.

CONFIDE was cleared for marketing by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration on May 14, 1996. The service was introduced initially in Texas and Florida in June of 1996, before the national rollout in September.
Direct Access stopped shipping the product today and is asking retail and wholesale customers to remove shelf stocks immediately and return all inventories, Johnson & Johnson said in a statement.
CONFIDE test results will continue to be processed until August 8 to serve any client who had purchased CONFIDE on or before June 26, but had not yet sent in a test card.
Anybody submitting test cards after August 8 and subsequently calling for their result will be informed of steps they can take to obtain a refund.
The CONFIDE Result Center will continue to operate until August 29, 1997 in order to transmit results and provide counseling and referral services, Johnson & Johnson said.

Anyone calling the CONFIDE Result Center after August 29 will automatically be directed to the National AIDS Hotline, operated by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, for information on local counseling services.
Johnson & Johnson would not disclose the costs of withdrawing the home HIV test, but it would not materially affect the company, spokesman Jeffrey Leebaw said.
About 60 jobs will be affected between next week and the end of the year, but attempts will be made to place them within other Johnson & Johnson companies, Leebaw said.
